artists.biography: Phil Cook is an American guitarist, banjoist, pianist and singer. He is a vocalist and multi-instrumentalist in the freak-folk band Megafaun. Before he became a member of Megafaun, Cook was part of DeYarmond Edison. Read more on Last.fm. perplexity.description:
Phil Cook’s Southland Mission, released in 2015 on Thirty Tigers, is a vibrant blend of rock, blues, folk, and country that reflects Cook’s deep roots in American roots music. The album showcases his signature style—warm, soulful, and steeped in tradition—while incorporating his own exploratory sensibilities. Tracks like “Ain’t It Sweet,” “1922,” and “Lowly Road” highlight his skillful use of banjo, piano, and slide guitar, weaving together elements of bluesgrass, southern rock, and gospel. The result is a sound that feels both timeless and fresh, drawing on the spirit of the American South while remaining distinctly personal.

Southland Mission stands as Cook’s second solo album, following his earlier work Hungry Mother Blues and his collaborative projects with bands like Megafaun and DeYarmond Edison. It marks a pivotal moment in his career, consolidating his reputation as a leading figure in the folk and Americana scenes. The album was praised for its authenticity and musicality, with critics noting its rich textures and Cook’s ability to balance tradition with innovation. It has been described as a prime example of “the John Kamman sound,” and received positive reviews for its heartfelt songwriting and dynamic performances.
